svg.text: PR #1957: two ways an RTP-level USER_PACING frame leaves in a burst
The area of each bar is the 4320 packets of one 1080p59.94 frame; its width is the time the RX side took to get them. Measured on E830 VFs, TSC pacing.
1. Without EXACT, a TAI more than 1 s ahead: the frame goes out at once, unpaced
st20_api.h of the PR: "Otherwise the frame goes on the epoch nearest to tai, even if that epoch is past or more than 1s ahead".
What the API says
now
1.5 s later (not to scale)
nearest epoch
4320 packets at TRS = 3.7 us: 16 002 us
the session waits for the epoch
What the NIC sent
now
nearest epoch: nothing left to send
tv_sync_pacing(): start = now + 1.5 s
video_trs_tsc_tasklet(): delta > NS_PER_S
-> err("invalid tsc cur .. target ..")
-> video_trs_burst() now, for each bulk
Seen in one run
frame 50: RX span 2 977.5 us, a paced frame 16 002 us (5.4x)
1080 err() lines for that frame, one per bulk of 4 packets
the stream does not stop for 1.5 s; frame 51 is on time
2. With EXACT, a fallback frame after an off-grid TAI starts while the frame before it is still on the wire
A frame with no TAI (or a TAI in the past or > 1 s ahead) gets default pacing: the epoch after the nearest epoch of the frame before it.
With an app TAI below 0.5 TFRAME that epoch is N+1, and its start is earlier than the end of frame N.
epoch N
epoch N+1
epoch N+2
frame N: EXACT at app TAI = N + 0.37 TFRAME, paced, 16 002 us
app TAI of frame N
default start of frame N+1: N+1 + TROFFSET - VRX x TRS
overlap 4.9 ms
frame N+1, then paced
catch-up burst
Frame N+1: first packet 5 501 us after epoch N+1 (paced: 615 us).
RX span 14 111 us, not 16 003 us: about 1.9 ms of its packets
leave faster than TRS. Seen for frames 30, 40 and 50 of the EXACT run.
Why
tv_sync_pacing() keeps cur_epochs = nearest epoch of the EXACT TAI (N for 0.37 TFRAME).
calc_frame_count_since_epoch() then gives the next frame N+1, and transmission_start_time()
puts it at N+1 + TROFFSET - VRX x TRS, 0.73 TFRAME after frame N started.
Why a burst is a fault: ST 2110-21:2022 §6.6.2 (p11) and §7.1.2 (p12)
A Type N sender passes the Virtual Receiver Buffer model: the VRXFULL bucket drains packet j at TPRj and must not overflow or underflow.
For 1080p59.94 with 4320 packets: VRXFULL = MAX(INT(1500 x 8 / 1500), INT(4320 / (27000 x TFRAME))) = 9 packets,
CMAX = MAX(4, INT(4320 / (43200 x 1080/1125 x TFRAME))) = 6 (§6.6.1, p9). Fault 1 sends the frame 1.5 s before its TPR0; fault 2 is late, then bursts.
Unit tests that fail on the PR: tests/unit/session/st20_tx/rtp_user_pacing_bugs_test.cpp. Sample: app/sample/low_level/tx_rtp_user_pacing_sample.c.
